primaryText: I met with someone at 19 hours.
comment: The book gives the Russian original; the English gloss is its translation, with the referent known to the speaker.

primaryText: John is looking for some book on reserve (*and I know which one).
comment: Determiner some marks the referent as unknown to the speaker, unlike someone and something.

primaryText: Do you think those men want to do some work?
context: Because my road needs to be repaired.
comment: The speaker expects a positive answer, so some is used.

primaryText: Do you think those men want to do any work?
context: Because they have been standing around all morning telling dirty jokes.
comment: The speaker expects a negative answer, so only any can be used.

primaryText: I promise you that, if you eat some (*any) spinach, I'll give you ten dollars.
I warn you that, if you eat any (*some) candy, I'll whip you.
Have you heard anything new about the ozone hole?
If you tell anybody, we'll punish you.
We doubt that Juan applied anywhere.
comment: The complement of an implicitly negative verb.

primaryText: Hannu is getting by without doing anything.
comment: The argument of an implicitly negative adposition.

primaryText: The boy can run faster than anyone in his class.
comment: The standard of comparison of inequality.

primaryText: The boy runs as fast as anyone in his class.
comment: The standard of comparison of equality.

primaryText: He didn't do anything to help her.
After the fall of the Wall, East Germans were free to travel anywhere.
I noticed nothing.
Ich habe etwas/irgend etwas verloren, aber ich weiss nicht, was.
translation: I lost something, but I don't know what.

primaryText: Sie möchte jemanden/irgend jemanden mit schwarzen Haaren heiraten.
translation: She wants to marry someone (non-specific or specific) with black hair.

primaryText: Hast du (irgend) etwas gehört?
translation: Did you hear anything?

primaryText: Ist sie irgend-wann/je in Chittagong gewesen?
translation: Has she ever been to Chittagong?

primaryText: Wenn (irgend) jemand anruft, sag mir Bescheid!
translation: If anyone calls, tell me!

primaryText: Ich glaube nicht, dass hier je/irgend-wann (irgend) jemand war.
translation: I don't think that anyone has ever been here.

primaryText: Joan Baez sang besser als IRGEND JEMAND JE zuvor.
translation: Joan Baez sang better than anyone ever before.
comment: Only the irgend-series and je are possible in the comparative; the irgend-indefinite must be stressed.

primaryText: Dieses Problem kann IRGEND JEMAND lösen.
translation: This problem can be solved by anyone.
comment: Stressed; jeder is generally preferred.

primaryText: Dieses Problem kann jeder lösen.
translation: This problem can be solved by anyone.

primaryText: Joan Baez singt besser als jede andere Sängerin.
translation: Joan Baez sings better than any other singer.

primaryText: ohne jede/irgend-welche Hilfe
translation: without any help
comment: The indirect-negation use is what makes jeder an indefinite rather than only a distributive universal.

primaryText: Sie stritt jede/irgend-eine Beteiligung ab.
translation: She denied any participation.

primaryText: Niemand ist gekommen.
translation: Nobody has come.
comment: The n-series does not co-occur with verbal negation.

primaryText: Ich habe niemandem (irgend) etwas gesagt.
translation: I didn't tell anything to anybody.

primaryText: Qualcuno è venuto—indovina chi!
translation: Someone has come—guess who!

primaryText: Non trovo la penna, eppure in qualche parte l'avrò messa.
translation: I can't find the pen, and yet I must have put it somewhere.

primaryText: Compra qualcosa per me.
translation: Buy something for me.
comment: Imperative.

primaryText: Vedi qualcosa/niente?
translation: Can you see anything?
comment: The nessuno-series is possible in questions but not in conditionals.

primaryText: Se senti qualcosa (*niente), svegliami.
translation: If you hear anything, wake me up.

primaryText: Non è necessario che venga nessuno/che qualcuno venga.
translation: It is not necessary that anyone come.

primaryText: Puoi andare dovunque.
translation: You can go anywhere.

primaryText: Christie ha scritto più romanzi che chiunque altro in questo secolo.
translation: Christie has written more novels than anyone else in this century.

primaryText: Non ho veduto nulla.
translation: I have not seen anything.
comment: Postverbal negative pronoun with verbal negation.

primaryText: Nessuno (*non) è venuto.
translation: Nobody has come.
comment: Preverbal negative pronoun without verbal negation.

primaryText: Nessun professore ha scritto mai nessun libro.
translation: No professor has ever written any book.

primaryText: Kto-to postučal v dver'.
translation: Somebody knocked at the door.

primaryText: Spojte nam kakoj-nibud'/kakoj-libo romans.
translation: Sing some romance for us.
comment: Imperative.

primaryText: My vstretimsja gde-nibud'/gde-libo.
translation: We'll meet somewhere.
comment: Future.

primaryText: Zvonil li mne kto-nibud'/kto-libo?
translation: Did anyone call me?

primaryText: Esli čto-nibud'/čto-libo slučitsja, ja skažu mame.
translation: If anything happens, I'll tell mom.

primaryText: Ona xočet vyjti zamuž za kogo-to iz Ameriki.
translation: She wants to marry someone (specific) from America.
comment: In an irrealis context the -to-series tends strongly towards the specific reading.

primaryText: Ona xočet vyjti zamuž za kogo-nibud'/kogo-to iz Ameriki.
translation: She wants to marry someone (non-specific) from America.
comment: The non-specific reading of -to seems possible, but -nibud' is clearly preferred.

primaryText: Zdes' prijatnee žit' čem gde-libo/gde by to ni bylo v mire.
translation: Here it is more pleasant to live than anywhere in the world.
comment: -nibud' is not possible in the comparative or indirect-negation functions.

primaryText: Otsutstvujut kakie-libo/kakie by to ni bylo ukazanija o sposobe ix primenenija.
translation: Any indications about the mode of their use are lacking.

primaryText: bez kakoj-libo/kakoj by to ni bylo pomošči
translation: without any help

primaryText: Esli ty uslyšiš' čto by to ni bylo, razbudi menja.
translation: If you hear anything (at all), wake me up.
comment: An emphatic variant in conditionals.

primaryText: *Slyšala li ty čto by to ni bylo?
translation: Did you hear anything (at all)?
comment: The by to ni bylo-series is not possible in questions.

primaryText: Ty možeš' kupit' ljubuju/kakuju ugodno/?kakuju by to ni bylo knigu.
translation: You may buy any book.
comment: The determiner ljuboj or the ugodno-series; by to ni bylo only marginally.

primaryText: Nikogda ja ne zabudu tebja.
translation: I will never forget you.
comment: Only the ni-series is possible under direct negation.

primaryText: Nam nado pogovorit' s toboj koe o čem.
translation: You and I have to talk about something.

primaryText: Kisii-ne (*bhii) fon kiyaa thaa, par mai tumhe nahii bataaugii, kis-ne. / par mujhe nahii maaluum, kis-ne.
translation: Someone has phoned, but I won't tell you who. / but I don't know who.
comment: Specific known and specific unknown alike; the bhii-series is excluded.

primaryText: Mujhe nahii lagtaa hai ki kal koii (bhii) aaegaa.
translation: It doesn't seem to me that anyone will come tomorrow.

primaryText: Ghar me koii (bhii) nahii hai.
translation: No one (at all) is at home.
comment: Under direct negation the bhii-series seems to be preferred.

primaryText: Kisii-ne kuch nahii dekhaa.
translation: Nobody saw anything. (Or: Someone saw nothing.)

primaryText: Wah kisii-ko/kisii-ko bhii fon karnaa caahtii hai.
translation: She wants to phone someone (specific or non-specific).
comment: In irrealis contexts the bhii-series is always non-specific.

primaryText: Kisii-ko (bhii) fon karo!
translation: Phone someone!

primaryText: Kyaa aap-ne kisii-ko/kisii-ko bhii dekhaa?
translation: Did you see somebody/anybody?
comment: The bhii-series is more emphatic in questions and conditionals.

primaryText: Agar koii (bhii) fon kare, mujhe bataanaa.
translation: If anybody (at all) calls, tell me.

primaryText: Yeh larkaa apne vidyaalay ke kisii bhii larke se zyaadaa tez daurtaa hai.
translation: This boy runs faster than anyone in his class.
comment: The comparative and free-choice functions are expressed only by the bhii-series.

primaryText: Ghar me koii bhii aa saktaa hai.
translation: Anyone can come into the house.

primaryText: Sana biri(si) telefon etti. Bil, bakalım, kim.
translation: Someone phoned you. Guess who.
comment: Only the bir-series is possible in the specific-known function.

primaryText: Sana biri(si)/herhangi biri telefon etti. Kim olduğunu bilmiyorum.
translation: Someone phoned you. I don't know who.

primaryText: Herhangi bir yere/bir yere telefon et!
translation: Call somewhere (or other)!

primaryText: Herhangi bir şey/bir şey/hiç bir şey duydun mu?
translation: Did you hear anything?

primaryText: Herhangi biri/biri telefon ederse, bana hemen söyle.
translation: If anyone calls, tell me immediately.

primaryText: Kimsenin/herhangi birinin/hiç kimsenin gelmesi gerekli değil.
translation: It is not necessary for anyone to come.

primaryText: Hiç bir şey/herhangi bir şey/bir şey görmedim.
translation: I didn't see anything.
comment: The hiç-indefinites are the most usual form and always co-occur with verbal negation.

primaryText: Herhangi biri bu problemi çözebilir.
translation: Anyone can solve this problem.
comment: Only the herhangi-series is possible in the free-choice and comparative functions.

primaryText: Murat sınıfındaki herhangi birinden daha hızlı koşar.
translation: Murat runs faster than anyone in his class.

primaryText: Valahol már találkoztunk.
translation: We have met somewhere before.

primaryText: Mester, láttunk valakit, a ki a te neveddel ördögöket űz.
translation: Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name.
comment: New Testament, Mark 9:38.

primaryText: Majd csak megleszünk valahogy.
translation: We'll manage somehow.

primaryText: Nem láttam semmit (*akármit, *bármit).
translation: I did not see anything.
comment: The sem-series can only be used under direct negation.

primaryText: Senkinek semmit sem szólának.
translation: Neither said they any thing to any man.
comment: New Testament, Mark 16:8.

primaryText: Akárki tanulhatott.
translation: Anybody could learn.

primaryText: Itt jobb a klíma, mint akárhol/bárhol Európában.
translation: Here the climate is better than anywhere in Europe.

primaryText: Nem hiszem, hogy valaki/bárki/akárki látta volna.
translation: I don't think that anybody has seen it.

primaryText: Ha bármit/akármit/valamit hallasz, ébressz fel.
translation: If you hear anything (at all), wake me up.
comment: The akár- and bár-series have an emphatic value in conditionals.

primaryText: Hallottál valamit (*akármit, *bármit)?
translation: Did you hear anything?
comment: The akár- and bár-series cannot be used in questions.

primaryText: *Joku soitti. Arvaa kuka (se oli)?
translation: Someone called. Guess who (it was).
comment: The -kin-series is excluded from the specific-known function.

primaryText: Eräs ystäväni kertoi sen.
translation: A certain friend told him.

primaryText: Joku soitti, mutta en saanut nimestä selvää.
translation: Someone called, but I didn't understand the name.

primaryText: Hän haluaa mennä naimisiin jonkun kanssa, jolla on tumma tukka.
translation: She wants to marry someone (non-specific) with black hair.

primaryText: Soittiko joku/kukaan/*kuka hyvänsä?
translation: Did someone/anyone call?
comment: The hyvänsä-series is impossible in questions.

primaryText: Jos joku/kuka hyvänsä/*kukaan soittaa, sano minulle.
translation: If someone/anyone at all calls, tell me.
comment: The -kaan-series is impossible in conditionals.

primaryText: Kukaan ei kertonut minulle mitään.
translation: Nobody told me anything.
comment: With verbal negation.

primaryText: Epäilen että poika varasti mitään.
translation: I doubt that the boy stole anything.

primaryText: Ilmasto on täällä miellyttävämpi kuin missään muualla Euroopassa.
translation: Here the climate is more pleasant than anywhere in Europe.
comment: The standard of comparison of inequality.

primaryText: Kuka tahansa osaa ratkaista tämän ongelman.
translation: Anyone can solve this problem.

primaryText: Täällä on yhtä mukavaa kuin missä tahansa muualla.
translation: It is as pleasant here as anywhere else.
comment: The standard of equative comparison only, as the map predicts from the conditional use.

primaryText: Mtu alinigusa.
translation: Somebody has touched me.
comment: New Testament, Luke 8:46; the book labels the example simply specific.

primaryText: Ana neno la kumwarifu.
translation: She has something to tell him.
comment: The book labels the example simply specific.

primaryText: Yesu alimwambia ... kwamba awape maskini kitu.
translation: Jesus told him to give something to the poor.
comment: New Testament, John 13:29.

primaryText: Waona kitu?
translation: Do you see anything?
comment: New Testament, Mark 8:23.

primaryText: Kama mtu akiwaambia neno, semeni, Bwana ana haja nao.
translation: If anyone says anything to you, say, the Lord needs them.
comment: New Testament, Matthew 21:3.

primaryText: Tokea hapo haijasikiwa ya kuwa mtu ameyafumbua macho ya kipofu.
translation: Since the world began was it not heard that any man opened the eyes of one that was born blind.
comment: New Testament, John 9:32.

primaryText: Wala hawakumwambia mtu neno.
translation: And they did not say anything to anybody.
comment: New Testament, Mark 16:8; bare generic nouns only postverbally under direct negation.

primaryText: Daktari yule ataponya magonjwa yo yote.
translation: That doctor will cure any disease whatsoever.

primaryText: Ninyi hamjui neno lo lote.
translation: You don't know anything.
comment: New Testament, John 11:49.

primaryText: Alimwambia malaika yupi wakati wo wote, Ndiwe mwanangu?
translation: To which of the angels did he ever say, You are my son?
comment: New Testament, Hebrews 1:5; a rhetorical question, with emphatic value.

primaryText: Mkiniomba neno lo lote kwa jina langu, nitalifanya.
translation: If you ask anything in my name, I will do it.
comment: New Testament, John 14:14.

primaryText: Movida vi-yac (*vin-me) rusi.
translation: Some Russian person has come (I don't know them).
comment: The -yac-series is restricted to the specific functions.

primaryText: Es c'igni sad-me unda vipovo.
translation: I have to find this book somewhere.

primaryText: Mosula vin-me (*vi-yac)?
translation: Has anyone come?

primaryText: Tu vin-me movides, utxari.
translation: If anyone comes, tell (me).

primaryText: Man kartuli ena uk'et icis vidre sxva vin-me-m.
translation: He knows Georgian better than anyone else.

primaryText: Mas ara-vis-tvis utkvams.
translation: He hasn't told anybody.
comment: One of the three negative series, normally with verbal negation.

primaryText: Chī diǎn shénme zài zǒu ba!
translation: Please eat a little something before you leave.
comment: Imperative.

primaryText: Tā hǎoxiàng xǐhuan shénme.
translation: He seems to like something.
comment: A context of uncertainty or inference.

primaryText: Shéi xǐhuan tā ma?
translation: Does anyone like him?

primaryText: Tā bù xǐhuan shénme.
translation: He does not like anything.
comment: Under direct negation only shénme is perfect; shéi is less acceptable.

primaryText: ?Tā bù xǐhuan shéi.
translation: He does not like anyone.

primaryText: Yǒu rén dǎ diànhuà le. (Wǒ bù zhīdào shì shéi. / Cāi yi cāi shì shéi.)
translation: Someone called. (I don't know who. / Guess who.)
comment: Bare interrogatives are not admissible in specific contexts that lack an element of uncertainty.

primaryText: Tā shéi-dōu bù xìnrèn.
translation: She doesn't trust anyone.
comment: The dōu- and yě-series occur only preverbally and are used interchangeably.

primaryText: Shéi-dōu bù cōngming.
translation: No one is intelligent.

primaryText: Rènhé shíhou nǐ dōu kěyǐ lái.
translation: You can come anytime.
comment: Mainly in conjunction with the adverb dōu.

primaryText: Tā pǎo de bǐ rènhé yíge nánshēng dōu kuài.
translation: He runs faster than any boy.

primaryText: Tā bù néng táo dào rènhé dìfang qù.
translation: He cannot escape anywhere.

primaryText: Wǒ bù xiāngxìn rènhé rén lái le.
translation: I don't think that anyone came.

primaryText: Pi-wan-chi qanyan awtobus-chaw parla-rqu-u.
translation: I talked to someone on the bus yesterday.

primaryText: Mana musya-pti-iki-qa pi-ta-pis tapuku-y.
translation: If you don't know, ask somebody.
comment: Imperative.

primaryText: Ima-ta-pis rika-rqu-nki-ku?
translation: Did you see anything?

primaryText: Ima-ta-pis rika-r-qa willa-ma-y.
translation: If you see anything, tell me.

primaryText: Pi-pis kay problema-ta-qa atinman-mi.
translation: Anyone can solve this problem.

primaryText: Pi-pis ni ima-ta-pis ni-ma-rqa-n-tsu.
translation: Nobody told me anything.
comment: The scope of negation is marked by the discontinuous negators.

primaryText: Mana muna-shkaa-chu pi-pis musyanan-ta.
translation: I didn't want anyone to know.

primaryText: Dare-ka kara denwa at-ta kedo, dare kara da ka wakara-na-i. / dare kara da ka ate-te goran.
translation: Someone called; I don't know who. / guess who!
comment: Specific unknown and specific known alike.

primaryText: Dare-ka ni ki-ite mi-masyoo.
translation: Let's ask somebody.
comment: Hortative.

primaryText: Rusutyuu-ni dare-ka (*dare-mo) ki-masi-ta ka?
translation: Did somebody/anybody come while I was gone?

primaryText: Nani-ka (*nani-mo) tabe-tara, eiga e ture-te it-te age-na-i yo.
translation: If you eat something/anything, I won't take you to the movie.

alternatives.form: Nani-mo tabe-tara, eiga e ture-te it-te age-na-i yo.

primaryText: Kono syoonen-wa kono kurasu-no dare-yori-mo hayaku hasir-u.
translation: This boy can run faster than anyone in his class.

primaryText: Dare-mo kanojo-o aisi-te i-na-i.
translation: Nobody loves her.
comment: With verbal negation.

primaryText: Kyoo-wa dare-mo ku-ru to omow-ana-i.
translation: I don't think anybody is coming today.

primaryText: Dare-demo deki-masu.
translation: Anybody can do it.

primaryText: Nwu-ka/nwukwu-inka-ka kel-ess-ta.
translation: Somebody called. (I didn't catch her name. / Guess who.)
comment: Specific unknown and specific known alike.

primaryText: Molu-myen, nwukwu-eykey/nwukwu-nka-eykey mul-ela.
translation: If you don't know, ask somebody.
comment: Imperative.

primaryText: Ku sonye-ka mues-ul/mue-nka-lul (*mues-ina/*mues-itunci) chac-umyen, kunye emeni-eykey malha-lkesi-ta.
translation: If the girl finds anything, she will tell her mother.
comment: The free-choice series are excluded.

primaryText: Chelswu mues-ul/mue-nka-lul (*mues-ina/*mues-itunci) ilk-ess-ni?
translation: Did Chelswu read anything?
comment: The free-choice series are excluded.

primaryText: Nwukwu-na/nwukwu-tunci/amu-na/amu-tunci i muncey-lul phul swu-iss-ta.
translation: Anybody can solve this problem.
comment: The -na- and -tunci-series are used interchangeably in the free-choice function.

primaryText: Nwukwu-to/nwukwu-lul/nwukwu-nka-lul chacki-ka pulkanung ha-ta.
translation: It's impossible to find anyone.
comment: Under indirect negation the bare interrogatives and the -nka-series are also possible.

primaryText: Ku sonye-nun amu-to/nwukwu-to an po-ass-ta.
translation: The girl did not see anybody.
comment: With verbal negation.

primaryText: Yeki-ka enu kos pota-to te alumtap-ta.
translation: Here it is more beautiful than anywhere.
